assistance_definition: M: one mandatory `pilot.py muse` call at CHECKPOINT A (after pkginfo, before any source reading or code); the response is shown to the operator, who records accepted/modified/rejected; up to 2 further optional calls. D: the same checkpoint with a written plan and no model.
checkpoint_text: a. Write down your plan, based on the documentation you have read: `.venv/bin/python research_tools/onboarding/pilot.py note --session "{SESSION}" intervention --detail "CHECKPOINT_A plan: <one-line plan>"`. Condition D has no model assistance.

design.contamination_controls: worktrees from the pre-onb-pilot/2 base f82e90d plus this manifest; an instruction not to read outside the worktree except the pinned sdists; identical frozen instructions apart from the checkpoint
design.contamination_limits: the same model family as earlier operators; filesystem isolation by instruction only; the main repository (outside the worktree) holds onb-pilot/2's adapters for these apps
design.pairing: each app under both D and M, separate fresh agent contexts, separate fresh worktrees from a base commit that holds no earlier adapter for these apps
design.replicates: 2 per (app, condition); each replicate's four sessions start together

label: AI-OPERATOR, NONBLIND EXPLORATORY: fresh AI agent contexts with no task-specific memory; not independent human participants; the two applications were already exposed by onb-pilot/2

measures.censoring: an unmet milestone is censored at the budget, never imputed
measures.checkpoint: CHECKPOINT_A notes (decision and reason); Muse calls, tokens, USD; Muse-sourced proposals and their validation
measures.per_session: session.measure (unchanged), plus: database-lock waiting time from the session's pg_lock.log, subtracted from every elapsed time it falls inside (pilot2_analyze.py); interventions; failed attempts; adapter lines final and revised; code revisions (snapshots with a changed adapter); rejected proposals; S2/S3 verification outcomes; Muse calls, tokens, est. USD

success.S3: the first S2 run where the harness recorder saw every enqueued key handled exactly once and every step finished without an exception
